newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks fall 2.17 pct on baht weakness.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks fall 2.17 pct on baht weakness.

text.p: Thai stocks extended a sharp descent on Tuesday in tandem with the baht's weakness and losses of regional currencies, traders said.
By 0442 GMT the SET Index had fallen 13.12 points or 2.17 percent to 591.22. The SET 50 fell 1.14 points or 2.51 percent to 44.22.
Brokers said sentiment was also affected by concerns over infighting within the ruling coalition government and weak economic fundamentals.
"The baht seems to be the main factor but political infighting doesn't help," said a broker at a major local firm.
The baht was quoted at 32.45/32.50 to the dollar onshore at 0456 GMT, slightly firmer than an intraday low of 32.60.

Squabbling within the core party in the ruling coalition government stemming from the removal of education minister Sukavit Rangsitphol, political uncertainty ahead of a parliamentary vote on Thailand's new constitution next month and the deterioration of the economy have all hurt sentiment, analysts said.
